Body:
I was able to reproduce this on `v2.0.15` (built from the tag), but the config in the issue as written doesn't trigger it on its own.

**The literal config doesn't reach the AI SDK path.** `aisdk:@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` matches the rewrite table in `AISDKNative.rewrite()` (`packages/core/src/aisdk-native.ts`), so it gets routed to `@opencode/ai/providers/openai-compatible`. The request comes out identical to the native route (correct `image_url`, no `"Attached media from tool result:"` text).

**A version-pinned specifier does reproduce it.** Both of these skip the rewrite, install `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible@3.0.57` at runtime, and send the `null` part:

```jsonc
"package": "aisdk:@ai-sdk/openai-compatible@3"
// or
"package": "aisdk:@ai-sdk/openai-compatible@latest"
```

```json
{"role":"tool","tool_call_id":"call_read_png","content":"[{\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":\"Image read successfully\"}]"}
{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Attached media from tool result:"},null]}
```

@krishna2206, did your config have a version suffix on the package, or something similar that avoided the rewrite?

**Cause.** `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` 3.x implements `specificationVersion: "v4"`, where a file part's `data` is a tagged object (`{ type: "data" | "url" | ... }`). `fileData()` in `packages/core/src/aisdk.ts` still returns the v3 shape (a raw base64 string / bytes / `URL`). The converter's `switch (part.data.type)` matches no case and returns `undefined`, which serializes to `null`. The same route with `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible@2.0.41` (the version the monorepo pins) sends a correct `image_url` part.

The JSON-encoded `tool` message content from the original report happens on both 2.0.41 and 3.0.57, so that one looks like a separate issue.

| package | tool-result image |
|---|---|
| `aisdk:@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` | rewritten to native, `image_url` ✅ |
| `aisdk:@ai-sdk/openai-compatible@3` / `@latest` (3.0.57) | `null` ❌ |
| AI SDK route with 2.0.41 | `image_url` ✅ |
| `@opencode/ai/providers/openai-compatible` | `image_url` ✅ |

**Suggested fixes:**
- Detect `specificationVersion` on AI SDK models and emit the v4 part shape (or reject v4 models with a clear error instead of silently sending `null`).
- Pin runtime installs of `aisdk:` packages to a compatible major when no version is given.

Repro (mock OpenAI-compatible server that logs request bodies and scripts a `read` call on a PNG, all six provider variants above): https://gist.github.com/JosvanderWesthuizen/b300022e40b6da969889ea579a2a03cd

This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #31423: Earlier request for the Desktop window title to reactively show the selected session and project.

Reproduction confirmed on the current stable build, with the mechanism isolated.

- App: OpenCode Desktop **2.0.18**, macOS 27.0 (arm64), Electron 44.4.3 / Chrome 152
- Repro: zoom in with `Cmd +`, quit fully, reopen → back to 100%

### The reset is an unguarded line in `wireZoom`

`packages/desktop/src/main/windows.ts` resets zoom on **every** window creation, with no guard:

```ts
function wireZoom(win: BrowserWindow) {
  pinchZoomEnabled.set(win, getPinchZoomEnabled())
  win.webContents.setZoomFactor(1)          // line 520 — unconditional
  ...
```

Note the asymmetry with line 528 in the same function, which *is* guarded:

```ts
if (win.webContents.getZoomFactor() !== 1) win.webContents.setZoomFactor(1)   // line 528
```

So the handler carefully avoids redundant resets, while window setup performs one unconditionally — discarding the persisted value before the UI settles.

### Chromium is persisting the zoom correctly

This is not a failure to save. `Preferences` contains a live per-origin entry:

```json
"partition": { "per_host_zoom_levels": { "12321934231736050979": { "renderer": 1.7967234568371628 } } }
```

That value tracks my zoom gestures precisely (it changed from 1.8454 to 1.7967 across sessions). Chromium restores it, and the app then overwrites it.

### Visible signature

At launch the shell renders large, then shrinks to 100% — the restored zoom is briefly visible before `wireZoom` clobbers it. This is observable and may be a useful regression-test signal.

### Enabling Pinch Zoom does not help

Turning on Settings → General → Pinch Zoom (`pinchZoomEnabled: true` is written to `opencode.settings` correctly) only affects the `zoom-changed` handler. It cannot undo the unconditional reset at line 520, so zoom still returns to 100% after restart. This is distinct from #49096 — here pinch zoom is *enabled*.

### No user-side workaround exists

- `ZOOM_FACTOR_KEY` / `zoomFactor` is absent from the 2.0.18 bundle, so pre-seeding `opencode.settings` has no effect.
- The menu (`view.zoomIn` / `view.zoomOut`) and keyboard paths call the same setter with no store write.
- No `OPENCODE_ZOOM` env var or zoom config field exists.

### Note

PR #50169 ("fix(desktop): persist zoom across app restarts") appears to address this and is currently CI-green and mergeable, but unreviewed. Flagging in case that helps it get picked up.

Confirming this on **2.0.18**, and the affected client is the **desktop app**, not the TUI. Also: **the collision matrix understates the blast radius** — WSL2 `networkingMode=nat` with `localhostForwarding=true` (the default) collides too.

## Still present on 2.0.18, via the desktop app

Same root cause, three additions worth folding in.

**1. The OpenCode Desktop (Electron) client fails the same way, and the real error never surfaces to the UI.** The desktop spawns its own bundled `opencode-cli.exe serve --service` and retries in the same loop, but the only thing the user ever sees is a fatal renderer error:

```
Error: Desktop IPC handler failed
Caused by:
{ "name": "Error", "message": "Timed out waiting for the background service to start" }
```

The actionable `Managed service port 49374 ... is already in use` text stays in the log. A desktop user has no `opencode service set port` in their workflow, so this reads as "the app is just broken" rather than a port conflict.

**2. The collision matrix is wrong for NAT mode.** This row says NAT does not collide:

| WSL2 NAT default / Docker bridge / full VM | no |

With `networkingMode=nat` and `localhostForwarding=true`, WSL2 relays a WSL `127.0.0.1` listener to Windows `127.0.0.1` via `wslrelay.exe`, so the two **do** share that loopback. My `.wslconfig`:

```ini
[wsl2]
networkingMode=nat
dnsTunneling=true
firewall=true
autoProxy=true
localhostForwarding=true
```

The WSL service and the Windows desktop each believed they owned the port. From Windows:

```
$ Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort 49374 -State Listen
LocalAddress LocalPort State  OwningProcess
127.0.0.1    49374     Listen 9296

$ Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter 'ProcessId=9296'
Name        CommandLine
wslrelay.exe  --mode 1 --vm-id {4d744808-...} --handle 1712
```

`wslrelay.exe` is the occupier, and its existence is the tell that this is WSL2 rather than a genuine second opencode client. From the WSL side the owner looks like an ordinary opencode process:

```
$ ss -tlnp | grep 49374
LISTEN 0 512 127.0.0.1:49374 users:(("opencode",pid=4771,fd=10))

$ ps -p 4771 -o args=
/home/<user>/.opencode/bin/opencode serve --service
```

So this is not a narrow mirrored-mode edge case — it is the **stock WSL2 configuration**, which is the common setup.

**3. Loop shape on 2.0.18.** 25 `cli starting` entries and 31 port-conflict failures across two desktop launches, ~10s apart, then the 120s timeout:

```
timestamp=2026-09-26T03:35:32.395Z level=INFO  message="cli starting" version=2.0.18 channel=latest local=false args="[\"serve\",\"--service\"]" role=cli
timestamp=2026-09-26T03:35:47.738Z level=ERROR message="cli process failed"
  cause="Cause([Fail(Error: Managed service port 49374 on 127.0.0.1 is already in use by another process.
  Configure another port with `opencode service set port <port>` and start the service again.
  (cause: ServeError (cause: Error: Failed to start server. Is port 49374 in use?)))])"
```

## Verified workaround

Move the **Windows** side off 49374, leaving WSL untouched. Moving WSL instead is the wrong direction here: the WSL service stays resident, and it is what feeds the loopback relay.

```
opencode service set port 49375
```

Writes `C:\Users\<user>\.config\opencode\service.json` → `{ "port": 49375 }`. Note the desktop's own `service get` was `{}` before this — the port was never configured on either side, both were silently taking the default.

Confirmed after the change:

```
v2 CLI background service ready { version: '2.0.18', probed: true, url: 'http://127.0.0.1:49375', port: '49375' }
```

Service ready in ~25ms instead of timing out at 120s, no `renderer.log` produced at all, and both ports coexist (49374 WSL relay + 49375 Windows). Manually starting the CLI also works and serves the UI:

```
$ opencode-cli.exe serve --service
server listening on http://127.0.0.1:49375
```

The hardcoded-default extraction in this issue still holds on 2.0.18 — `49374` appears as a string in the shi

If you believe this was flagged incorrectly, please let a maintainer know.

**Still present on 2.0.18** — confirming from a different platform, with the client-side record as evidence.

**Environment:** opencode **2.0.18** (CLI, Homebrew `opencode-v2`), macOS **27.0** (arm64), zsh, no plugins,
`opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash`, endpoint `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions`.

**Observed:** one session (started 2026-09-24 09:05 UTC) hit **7** `provider.invalid-request` 400s in ~3.5 h —
2026-09-25 23:48 → 2026-09-26 03:16 UTC: four on 2.0.16 (23:48, 00:02, 00:40, 00:59) and three after the upgrade on
**2.0.18** (01:29, 02:36, 03:16). Requests of the *same* size succeeded minutes either side (e.g. 534,912- and
535,040-token requests passed around the 03:16 failure), and the session had passed that size for the preceding two
days — so, as your byte-faithful replay shows, this is not a stable verdict on the payload. Continuing the turn always
recovered it; no session was bricked.

One sizing datapoint, to keep this distinct from a pure ceiling: the session did reach **967,680** cached prompt tokens
and a request at that size succeeded (2026-09-25 13:08), ~10 h before the failures — the 400s themselves were at
~350–535k, well below the ~968k figure in #50574.

**Persisted error record — confirming the body drop** (your Actual Behavior): on 2.0.18 the failed assistant message
carries only

```json
{"type":"provider.invalid-request","message":"Provider request failed with HTTP 400","status":400}
```

with no provider body, so nothing after the fact recovers the stub. To reproduce the record shape (read the DB with the
app running, or append `&immutable=1`):

```sh
sqlite3 "file:$HOME/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db?mode=ro" \
  "SELECT datetime(time_created/1000,'unixepoch'), json_extract(data,'\$.error') FROM session_message
   WHERE session_id='<ses_…>' AND json_extract(data,'\$.error') IS NOT NULL ORDER BY seq DESC LIMIT 5;"
```

Checked all four candidates — confirming the relationship of each rather than plain duplicate status:

**Same root-cause family as #39291 / #45456** (replayed reasoning/thinking state rejected by the provider on request rebuild), but this report differs on three axes:

1. **Trigger**: `SessionRunner.drain` resuming a pending step after a service restart — not compaction (#39291) and not a generic long-running-overflow case (#45456).
2. **Provider stack**: native Mistral integration (`@opencode/ai/providers/mistral`, `zai-glm-5-3`) with a Python-side backend error — `'str object' has no attribute 'items'`, i.e. a string arriving where a dict/object is expected — rather than Anthropic's byte-identical-thinking rejection or a bare `invalid_request_error`.
3. **Currency**: this still reproduces on server **v2.0.18** (latest release). #45456 was closed as completed in August, so this is evidence that the replay-sanitization gap persists into the current release on the drain path / for this provider's state shape.

**Not a duplicate of #46564** — that tracks the context-overflow classification gap (opaque 400 never engages one-shot compaction recovery). In our case normal sends carrying the same full session history succeed; only the drain-path replay is rejected, so it is not an overflow misclassification.

**Not a duplicate of #49740, but complementary** — that issue tracks the missing `session.error` surfacing for swallowed drain exceptions. Our case is another concrete instance of that silent dead-end (the client only sees repeated failures), but the cause analysis here is distinct. The retry cadence evidence (~15s, 13+ occurrences over ~7 minutes) is available for that report if useful.

Suggest keeping this open as the drain-path + native-Mistral data point unless maintainers prefer to consolidate under #39291 — in which case the two deltas worth carrying over are the drain-resume trigger and the v2.0.18 reproduction.

I read the current sources on both branches before touching this, and the two code paths cited in the report are from the default branch (`dev`), not from the 2.0.x line the report was filed against.

**Confirmed on `v2`** (root `package.json` is 2.0.18):
- The complaint holds. `packages/tui/src/component/prompt/autocomplete.tsx` builds the slash list in `commands()` at `:474-494`: keymap commands at `:475-483`, server commands at `:486-493`. Every option is `{ display, description, onSelect }`, so no entry carries or renders a source marker and built-in, custom, skill and MCP entries do look identical.

**Does not carry over to `v2`:**
- `packages/app/src/components/prompt-input/slash-popover.tsx`, cited as the badge precedent with `prompt.slash.badge.skill|mcp|custom`, does not exist on `v2`: the whole `packages/app/src/components/prompt-input/` directory is absent, and no `prompt.slash.badge.*` key exists in v2 `packages/ui/src/i18n/en.ts`.
- The described TUI mechanism (`source === "skill"` skipped, `":mcp"` suffix otherwise) sits at `dev` `packages/tui/src/component/prompt/autocomplete.tsx:451-452`. On `v2` there is no such branch, and there cannot be: `packages/schema/src/command.ts` on `v2` declares `Info = { name, description? }` with no `source` field.

**What that implies for scope:**
- On `v2` this is not a rendering tweak. It needs a `source` field on `Command.Info`, which is a public Protocol surface, and per `AGENTS.md` that also means regenerating the client from `packages/client` (`bun run generate`) plus new i18n keys. How to mark a source in a terminal list is also a design choice, so it seems worth agreeing the shape before implementing.
- Independently of the marker, the "skills have no presence at all" half may have a different cause on `v2`: the list comes from `data.location.command.list(...)`, so whether skills appear depends on what that endpoint returns.

If the report was actually taken from a 1.18.32 build rather than 2.0.16, the TUI half is much smaller, since `dev` already reads `source` there. Worth confirming which build, because the two lines need different changes.

Thanks for comparing them. That's the difference: #46023 makes concurrent writes safe, and this PR also stops `Auth.set` and `Auth.remove` from reading through `OPENCODE_AUTH_CONTENT`, which is how a workspace child drops credentials added after it was spawned. #46128 describes both failure modes.

@arul28 #42771 does the second thing you ask for. `summary.diffs[].patch` moves to a `message_diff` table, `message.updated` keeps only each file's name, status and line counts, and clients fetch a patch when the diff is expanded. On a 51 GB database, diff-carrying `message.updated` events dropped from about 433 KB to 4.4 KB on average (largest 60 MB → 2.3 MB), and it has been running on that machine since Aug 15.

@peterradzisz it also adds an opt-in `retention.event_idle_days`. Sessions idle longer than that lose their event history through the same `EventV2.remove` that deleting a session uses, which removes the session's events and its sequence row together, so it doesn't leave the sequence holes described above. It does nothing for sessions that stay active. With the patches gone, their events are small (about 1.2 KB per row on that machine now), but the table still grows with use.

Workaround for the v2 incompatibility, until the extension ships a fix (or a configurable command, as suggested above).

The extension launches the TUI with `vscode.window.createTerminal(...)` + `sendText("opencode --port <port>")`, i.e. it types the command into an interactive shell, so a shell **function** in `~/.zshrc` can rewrite it. It has to be a function, not an alias: alias expansion only replaces the first word, so `alias opencode='opencode serve'` would also mangle every `opencode run …` / `opencode api …` call.

```zsh
# ~/.zshrc — workaround for sst-dev.opencode (v0.0.13) on opencode v2
opencode() {
  if [[ "$1" == "--port" ]]; then
    shift 2   # v2 removed --port; attach to the shared background service
  fi
  command opencode "$@"
}
```
Verified on opencode v2.0.18 (macOS, zsh, extension v0.0.13):

A setting to override the launched command (previous comment) plus a shared-service/`--standalone` choice would be the proper fix.

## Investigation update — not an OpenCode defect

Further testing shows this is not caused by OpenCode (and not Electron-specific):

- Even a **standard-framed Electron test window** (no `autoHideMenuBar`, no custom title bar style) shows no menu bar / traffic lights on hover in fullscreen on this machine.
- A **native AppKit app (TextEdit) behaves identically** — same missing menu bar and traffic lights, so the behavior is OS-level, not an app/Electron bug.

The machine is running **macOS 27.0 (build 26A428)**, and the spaces configuration shows the "fullscreen" window is actually a **tiled window** (`TileSpaces` / `type = 5` in `com.apple.spaces`), i.e. macOS 26/27's new window tiling. In that tiled state the hover-to-reveal menu bar / traffic lights do not appear. This affects all apps (VS Code, Ollama, OpenCode, TextEdit) on this system.

**Workarounds / exits from fullscreen:** ⌃⌘F, or the green traffic light / menu bar in windowed mode. Notably, native TextEdit also exits fullscreen with **ESC** (an AppKit standard since Mojave); Electron does not replicate this, so ⌃⌘F is the only OpenCode way. Supporting ESC-to-exit-fullscreen on macOS could be tracked as a separate feature request if desired.

Closing as not an OpenCode bug.

The deadlock occurs because asynchronous permission requests from child subagents lack a completion timeout and cancellation propagation.

When a subagent requests access to an external directory, the request yields control to the supervisor. If the event channel between subagent and parent is interrupted or unhandled, the subagent thread blocks indefinitely on an unfulfilled promise. Because the parent marks the turn busy until the subagent completes, the entire session freezes and ignores user interrupts.

To resolve this pattern:
1. Wrap subagent tool executions in bounded contexts with monotonic timeouts.
2. Propagate parent abort signals directly to child process handles via `pidfd_send_signal`.
3. Default unresolved permission requests to a fast fail-closed verdict after a timeout, returning a structured error to the parent turn instead of hanging.

Same capability-discovery bug reproduces in a plain **CLI/TUI session** (not just web).

**Environment:** opencode v2.0.16, Linux x64, terminal (CLI), no plugins, no desktop app installed.

**Repro:**
1. `opencode` (TUI) / `opencode run`, no desktop app running.
2. Code Mode catalog includes `tools.browser.tabs.list`, `tools.browser.tabs.open`, `tools.browser.screenshot`, etc.
3. Call `tools.browser.tabs.open({url: ...})` →
   `[browser.disconnected] No desktop browser is connected to this session. Open this session in the desktop app and wait for it to connect.`

**Investigation (v2.0.16 binary + docs + live API):**
- V2 docs (Tools → Browser) say the namespace "controls the browser attached by the OpenCode desktop app" — no config field or setup page is documented.
- `/openapi.json` exposes **0** `browser` paths; the only attach path is the RPC `experimental.browser.attach` (`Browser.Control`, server-side `BrowserConnection`, keyed by `sessionID`) which must be called by a client that *hosts* the browser. The CLI has no such host.
- No `opencode browser` subcommand, and no `OPENCODE_*` experimental env var exists in the binary (`grep OPENCODE_*`: no `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL`), so there is no CLI-side switch.
- Attempted workarounds that do **not** help: `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL=true`, `opencode pair` (pairs clients to the server, doesn't attach a browser).

**Impact:** the model sees ~45 dead `browser.*` schema entries in every CLI session's catalog (wasted input tokens each turn) and can pick a tool that can never succeed.

**Suggested fix:** don't advertise the namespace when no browser-capable client is attached — or gate the catalog on an explicit config/permission opt-in.

**Workaround used locally:** `{"action":"browser","resource":"*","effect":"deny"}` in `permissions` removes the catalog (documented in Tools → Browser).

**The symptom here is a hard failure, not a silent one.** The desktop renderer dies during startup with a "server request failed — HTTP 500" screen, and the bundled service returns 500 on every directory-scoped endpoint:

```
cause="PlatformError: NotFound: FileSystem.realPath (<deleted dir>)

**The deleted path is persisted in two places**, and nothing in the product surfaces them:

1. Client — `~/Library/Application Support/ai.opencode.desktop/drafts.sqlite`, table `state`, document `opencode.global.dat`, key `layout` → `home.selection.directory`. This is what makes startup fatal. `server.projects.local[].worktree` in the same document also keeps the dead project in the sidebar.
2. Server — `opencode.db`, table `project`, column `worktree` (plus `session.directory` / `session_v2.directory` for that project's sessions).

If anyone is still waiting for a plugin, just made a V2 [plugin](https://github.com/malhashemi/opencode-dynamic-workflows), be aware this intentionally expands on CC capabilities, most high-risk additions are configurable

# Features

* Plain TypeScript: agent(), pipeline, parallel, loops and if.
* Shell, files and HTTP: `ctx.$`, `ctx.file` and `ctx.fetch`, confined to the project and logged in the Run's activity; can be turned off for agent-written Workflows.
* Typed results: give a Unit a zod schema and get a validated value back, not prose.
* Any model per Unit: mix models and agents in one Workflow.
* The agent can write Workflows: you read the whole script and approve it before it runs.
* Saved Workflows: each one becomes a slash command, and /workflows lists them.
* People in the loop: a Workflow can ask you questions mid-run, and you answer permission requests from the same place.
* Limits: concurrency caps and token budgets.
* Resume: every Unit is journaled, so a stopped or crashed Run resumes where it left off.
* TUI: Run library, phases, Units, transcripts; stop a Run, restart a Unit.
* Web app: the same views in a browser, served locally; pair other devices.
* Build on it: a versioned protocol with an OpenAPI 3.1 spec, so other apps can start and follow Workflows.

# Install

    opencode plugin add @malhashemi/opencode-dynamic-workflows
    opencode service restart

Needs OpenCode 2.0.16+.

_The following comment was made by an LLM, it may be inaccurate:_

Same failure here on **Firefox 156.0 (x86_64)** with opencode **v1.18.32** — web UI on a plain-HTTP origin accessed from another host over a WireGuard IP, so this isn't Chromium-specific. Firefox just words it differently:

```
Uncaught (in promise) TypeError: can't access property "digest", crypto.subtle is undefined
    putBlob → addAttachments
```

Attach button / drag-drop / paste: all silently discarded, message sends text-only.

A workaround for people who can't switch to `localhost` or put TLS in front (WG/Tailscale/LAN access): Firefox can mark specific hosts as secure contexts. Create `dom.securecontext.allowlist` in `about:config` as a **string** pref, set it to the server IP/hostname (comma-separated; host only — no scheme, no port; parsed in `dom/security/nsMixedContentBlocker.cpp`), restart the browser. `window.isSecureContext` becomes `true` on the same `http://<ip>:<port>` origin, `crypto.subtle` is available again, and attachments work end-to-end. Verified on the setup above.

Obviously still worth the client-side fallback (`getRandomValues` / pure-JS SHA-256) — the pref only helps Firefox users who control their own browser config.
